title: Launch tide: slate and telemetry habit tracker
content:
OVERVIEW
This is a working playpad for a small soft launch (tide) of the routing and telemetry changes in PR #1987. Purpose: validate observability coverage and low-risk traffic shaping before a wider miniwave. Focus areas: telemetry habit (what we measure every hour), minimal rollback surface, and an ops-friendly calendar for a weekday quiet window.

GOALS (primary)
- Confirm Canary level SLOs (P50 route latency <= 55ms, error rate < 0.5% for canary region)
- Verify new telemetry tags (route_variant, model_variant, kvcache_hit) are populated end-to-end
- Smoke test fallback behavior when dedicated pool saturates

GOALS (secondary)
- Collect token-cost delta for 24h sample
- Validate rollout comms templates and one-click rollback steps with oncall

ROLLOUT CALENDAR (UTC/PST notes)
- T-7d (2026-05-03): Draft + peer review (this doc). Owner: Elena Park.
- T-3d (2026-05-07 18:00 UTC / 11:00 PDT): Canary CI dry-run; smoke tests locally and on staging. Owner: Julian.
- T-1d (2026-05-09 20:00 UTC / 13:00 PDT): Preflight no-traffic rehearsal (feature flag off, run smoke). Owner: Priya.
- Launch day (2026-05-10): Quiet window 14:00–18:00 UTC / 07:00–11:00 PDT.
   - 14:00 UTC: Enable 1% traffic routing to new variant in region-us-west.
   - 14:15 UTC: Verify telemetry tags and dashboards.
   - 15:00 UTC: Increase to 5% if green.
   - 16:30 UTC: Evaluate metrics and decide to advance to 20% or rollback.
   - 17:45 UTC: Final decision to keep or rollback.
- Post-launch (T+1d..T+7d): Data collection & regression alerts review.

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (must be green before T-1d)
- [ ] PR #1987 merged to release branch and container image built and pushed (sha: TBD)
- [ ] Conformant feature flag (ff/route-tide) created with default OFF
- [ ] Canary config created: 1% -> 5% -> 20% transition with automatic halt on error budget
- [ ] Dashboards: canary-latency, canary-errors, kvcache-hit-rate, token-cost-diff created and linked
- [ ] Pager duty rotation: confirmed and contactable (list below)
- [ ] Runbook snippet available in #release-ops Slack and pinned in channel
- [ ] DB migration? NONE (confirm)

DAY-OF RUNBOOK (hour-by-hour notes)
- 13:30 UTC: Ops pre-brief — quick check on perf tests, infra capacity, SRE oncall introduced.
- 14:00 UTC: Flip ff/route-tide -> enable 1% in region-us-west. Post message: "Tide ON: 1% west".
- 14:05 UTC: Check canary-latency P50/P90 & canary-errors for spike; open live tail logs for route_variant label.
- 14:15 UTC: Verify kvcache_hit-rate >= baseline -3pt, and that tags are present in traces.
- 14:45 UTC: If OK, increase to 5%. If not OK, rollback immediately (see rollback steps).
- 15:00–16:00 UTC: Monitor for slow growth in error rate; check sampled request traces and function/tool calls.
- 16:30 UTC: Decision checkpoint: keep at 5% and plan next day ramp, or roll back.
- 17:45 UTC: Close the window: record notes, acknowledge todos in ticket RLSE-4821.

OBSERVABILITY SIGNALS (priority order)
1) Platform errors / 5xx spikes (high severity)
2) Canary error-rate (application errors)
3) Route latency skew (P50 / P90) between variant and baseline
4) KV cache hit rate; tag absence (indicates instrumentation fallout)
5) Token-cost-diff > +10% (investigate prompt expansion or encoding change)
6) Traces with new tags missing or malformed (low-level infra bug)

DASHBOARDS & TEMPLATES
- Dashboard names (create if missing): canary-latency, canary-errors, kvcache-hit-rate, token-cost-diff, rollout-health-summary
- Slack snippet to post when enabling: "[TIDE] enabling ff/route-tide -> 1% west. Oncall: @samir, @priya. Watch: canary-latency, canary-errors."
- Incident template: short summary, observed metric (value), time, rollback yes/no, root-cause hypothesis, action items.

SMOKE TESTS MATRIX (quick checks to run after each ramp)
- API basic flow: response schema unchanged, status 200 for 100 sample requests. (Test: smoke-api-basic)
- Function/tool calling: 10 requests with function call path exercised. (smoke-fncall)
- Cache behavior: seed warm KV cache and confirm kvcache_hit-rate > 30% in sample window. (smoke-cache)
- Fallback on saturation: artificially set pool capacity lower in staging and confirm fallback triggers. (smoke-fallback)

ROLLBACK (fast path — aim <=90s to target)
- Trigger: any of the top 3 signals breach thresholds for >5m.
- Steps: 1) Flip ff/route-tide -> OFF (console action) 2) Post rollback message to Slack channel with incident template 3) Revert any temporary infra knobs (if used) 4) Create follow-up ticket assigned to owners 5) If rollback successful, hold rollout for 24h and re-evaluate

COMMUNICATION PLAN
- Pre-launch: brief in #release-ops and add to daily standup notes.
- During: minute-level status updates at each ramp step by Release Conductor (Samir)
- Post-launch: short debrief in channel + update RLSE-4821 with data and decision

POST-LAUNCH (T+1..T+7)
- Collect full 24h telemetry and attach to ticket (token-cost, latencies, errors)
- Run small A/B evaluation on downstream quality metrics for 48h
- Schedule a short retro (30m) 72h after launch to capture learnings

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs
- Need definitive image sha and release tag (TODO: Julian to provide by T-1d).
- Confirm PR backport plan if immediate hotfix required (are there release branch constraints?).
- Is there any customer scheduled maintenance that overlaps the quiet window? (check calendar).
- Decide whether to enable extended tracing sampling for 2 hours after each ramp (cost impact).

RELEASE NOTES (draft)
Title: "Routing telemetry pilot: safer routing + richer observability (tide)"
Notable changes:
- Added a small-traffic routing variant that tags requests with route_variant and kvcache_hit; intended to validate new telemetry and fallback logic.
- Improved fallback behavior when dedicated pools approach capacity: automatic degrade to baseline variant.
Impact:
- Expected user-visible change: none for majority of traffic. Canary traffic: up to 20% in a single region during the pilot.
- Known limitations: token cost telemetry may undercount in early hours; monitoring configured to alert at +10% delta.
Migration notes:
- No client-side changes required. SDKs remain compatible.

NOTES TO SELF (informal)
- Keep the day-of comms short and frequent; ops gets drowned if verbose.
- If telemetry tags are missing, suspect build-time instrumentation or sidecar rollout order.

KNOWN LINKS / REFERENCES
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1987
- Ticket: RLSE-4821
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.internal/redwood/pages/RELEASE-2026-05

END OF PAD — record changes here as we iterate.
